name: CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark
description: The Center for Internet Security (CIS) Foundations Benchmark for Amazon Web Services provides prescriptive guidance for configuring AWS services securely. Covers IAM, logging, monitoring, networking, and storage.

controls.title: Ensure applications have designated owners (IAM accountability)
controls.description: Every application must have a designated owner for incident response, change approvals, and audit accountability.
controls.rationale: Without a designated owner, security incidents cannot be triaged efficiently, changes may be deployed without proper review, and audit trails become incomplete. CIS IAM controls require accountability for all managed resources.
controls.query: MATCH (a:Application) WHERE (a.owner IS NULL OR a.owner = '') RETURN a.id AS resourceId, a.name AS resourceName, 'Application' AS resourceType, 'No owner assigned' AS evidence

remediation.summary: Assign an owner to each application via the Applications page.
steps: Navigate to Applications → select the app without an owner
Set the Owner field to a team or named individual
Tag the underlying AWS resources with the appcloud:owner tag for future discovery runs
Document the ownership in your CMDB or team directory

controls.title: Ensure S3 buckets are not publicly accessible
controls.description: S3 buckets should not allow public read or write access unless explicitly required and justified.
controls.rationale: Public S3 buckets have been the source of numerous high-profile data breaches. Objects stored in public buckets are accessible to anyone on the internet, including threat actors scanning for sensitive data.
controls.query: MATCH (i:S3Bucket) WHERE i.public = true RETURN i.id AS resourceId, i.name AS resourceName, 'S3Bucket' AS resourceType, i.region AS evidence

remediation.summary: Enable S3 Block Public Access at the account and bucket level.
steps: Open the S3 console and navigate to the affected bucket
Go to Permissions → Block Public Access settings and enable all four options
Review and tighten the bucket policy to remove public principals
Enable S3 Block Public Access at the account level for defence in depth
Audit existing objects for sensitive data exposure

controls.title: Ensure RDS instances are not publicly accessible
controls.description: Relational database instances should not be accessible from the public internet. Use VPC peering, PrivateLink, or bastion hosts for access.
controls.rationale: Public RDS instances are exposed to credential-stuffing attacks and zero-day exploits. Databases often contain the crown jewels of an organisation and must be behind defence-in-depth controls.
controls.query: MATCH (i:RDSInstance) WHERE i.public = true RETURN i.id AS resourceId, i.name AS resourceName, 'RDSInstance' AS resourceType, i.region AS evidence

remediation.summary: Disable public accessibility on the RDS instance and move it to a private subnet.
steps: Open the RDS console and select the affected instance
Modify → Connectivity → set 'Publicly accessible' to No
Ensure the instance is in a private subnet with no internet gateway route
Configure security groups to allow traffic only from application subnets
For remote access, use a bastion host, Session Manager, or PrivateLink

controls.title: Ensure Tier-1 applications have deployment records for blast radius analysis
controls.description: All Tier-1 applications must have at least one component linked to deployed infrastructure so blast radius and incident impact can be determined.
controls.rationale: Without deployment records, the platform cannot determine which infrastructure to protect or which applications to notify during changes. This is foundational for CIS monitoring controls.
controls.query: MATCH (a:Application {tier: 1}) WHERE NOT (a)-[:CONTAINS]->(:Component)-[:DEPLOYED_ON]->(:Infra) RETURN a.id AS resourceId, a.name AS resourceName, 'Application' AS resourceType, 'Tier-1 app missing deployment' AS evidence

remediation.summary: Link the application to its deployed components.
steps: Run the Mapping agent from the Command Center to auto-link by tags
Add the appcloud:app tag to AWS resources that belong to this application
Re-run discovery to pick up the tags
Manually link remaining components via the Applications page if needed

controls.title: Ensure Tier-1 application components are not exposed on public infrastructure
controls.description: Business-critical (Tier-1) applications must not have components deployed directly onto public-facing infrastructure. Public components must be behind a load balancer, API gateway, or WAF.
controls.rationale: Direct public exposure of Tier-1 workloads dramatically increases attack surface. All inbound traffic to critical systems should flow through a layer that provides logging, rate limiting, and threat filtering.
controls.query: MATCH (a:Application {tier: 1})-[:CONTAINS]->(c:Component)-[:DEPLOYED_ON]->(i:Infra) WHERE i.public = true RETURN i.id AS resourceId, i.name AS resourceName, 'Infra' AS resourceType, a.name AS evidence

remediation.summary: Move Tier-1 components behind a managed edge service.
steps: Introduce an Application Load Balancer or API Gateway in front of the component
Move the component itself to a private subnet
Attach AWS WAF if the service accepts user input
Enable detailed access logging with anomaly alerting
Restrict security groups to accept traffic only from the ALB/APIGW security group

controls.title: Ensure high-risk changes affecting Tier-1 applications are explicitly approved
controls.description: Changes with risk score 7 or higher that affect Tier-1 applications must go through explicit approval workflow before deployment.
controls.rationale: Unapproved high-risk changes on critical systems bypass change management controls required by SOC 2 CC8.1, ISO 27001 A.12.1.2, and CIS change control guidelines. An unreviewed deployment to a Tier-1 system can cascade into a company-wide outage.
controls.query: MATCH (ch:Change {status: 'draft'})-[:AFFECTS]->(a:Application) WHERE ch.riskScore >= 7 AND a.tier = 1 RETURN ch.id AS resourceId, ch.title AS resourceName, 'Change' AS resourceType, 'Risk ' + toString(ch.riskScore) AS evidence

remediation.summary: Route the change through the approval workflow.
steps: Open the change on the Changes page
Submit for review by the application owner and on-call engineer
Obtain explicit approval before scheduling deployment
Document the rollback plan and deployment window
Only proceed after the change is in 'approved' status

controls.title: Ensure segregation of duties in change approvals (no self-approval)
controls.description: A user should not be able to submit and approve the same change. This enforces separation of duties and prevents unilateral production changes.
controls.rationale: Self-approval bypasses segregation-of-duties controls required by SOX, SOC 2 CC6.1, and PCI-DSS 6.4. It enables insider threats and accidental misconfigurations to reach production unchallenged.
controls.query: MATCH (u:User)-[:SUBMITTED]->(ch:Change)<-[:APPROVED]-(u) RETURN ch.id AS resourceId, ch.title AS resourceName, 'Change' AS resourceType, u.name AS evidence

remediation.summary: Rollback the approval and re-route the change to an independent reviewer.
steps: Void the self-approval on the change
Require a second reviewer (different from the submitter) before approval
Update RBAC policy to technically enforce the segregation-of-duties rule at the system level
Document the corrective action in the audit log

controls.title: Ensure load balancers that front Tier-1 apps are tracked for TLS posture
controls.description: Load balancers that serve Tier-1 workloads must be tracked so TLS certificates, cipher suites, and WAF associations can be evaluated. This control verifies that every Tier-1 app with public exposure has a load balancer in front.
controls.rationale: Tier-1 applications without a managed edge component (load balancer, CDN, API gateway) cannot enforce consistent TLS policy or WAF rules. CIS encryption-in-transit controls require a consistent TLS termination point.
controls.query: MATCH (a:Application {tier: 1})-[:CONTAINS]->(c:Component)-[:DEPLOYED_ON]->(i:Infra) WHERE i.public = true AND NOT (c)-[:CONNECTS_TO|DEPLOYED_ON]->(:AWSLoadBalancer) AND NOT (i:AWSLoadBalancer) RETURN a.id AS resourceId, a.name AS resourceName, 'Application' AS resourceType, 'No LB fronting public Tier-1 component' AS evidence

remediation.summary: Introduce a managed load balancer or CDN in front of public Tier-1 workloads.
steps: Provision an Application Load Balancer or CloudFront distribution
Terminate TLS at the load balancer with an ACM-managed certificate
Configure TLS 1.2+ only and modern cipher suites
Associate an AWS WAF web ACL for common attack protection
Update discovery to pick up the new load balancer and re-run mapping

controls.title: Ensure confidential data workloads are not on public infrastructure
controls.description: Applications classified as 'confidential' or 'restricted' must never be deployed on public-facing infrastructure, regardless of tier.
controls.rationale: Confidential or restricted workloads are subject to data-handling regulations (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS). Public exposure creates direct regulatory violations and data-breach risk.
controls.query: MATCH (a:Application)-[:CONTAINS]->(c:Component)-[:DEPLOYED_ON]->(i:Infra) WHERE i.public = true AND a.confidentiality IN ['restricted', 'confidential'] RETURN a.id AS resourceId, a.name AS resourceName, 'Application' AS resourceType, a.confidentiality AS evidence

remediation.summary: Move the workload to private infrastructure immediately.
steps: Migrate the workload to a private subnet or VPC
Audit data flow to confirm encryption at rest and in transit
Notify the security and compliance teams
Initiate a breach-assessment review if public access was recent
Review the data-handling policy for the application classification

controls.title: Ensure public-facing infrastructure has identifiable owning applications
controls.description: Every piece of public-facing infrastructure should be linked to an application so its purpose and owner are known.
controls.rationale: Orphan public infrastructure represents unknown attack surface. Resources without an owning application cannot be patched, monitored, or decommissioned safely.
controls.query: MATCH (i:Infra) WHERE i.public = true AND i.provider = 'aws' AND NOT (i)<-[:DEPLOYED_ON]-(:Component) RETURN i.id AS resourceId, i.name AS resourceName, i.resource_type AS resourceType, i.region AS evidence

remediation.summary: Identify and link orphan public infrastructure to an application.
steps: Investigate the resource — determine its purpose and whether it is still needed
If no longer needed, raise a decommissioning change
If needed, add the appcloud:app tag and re-run discovery + mapping
Review IAM and security group rules to restrict unintended access
